title: The magnificent ten: A coalition of the willing to drive the EU’s next enlargement – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: ECFR argues the EU has no strategy to admit Ukraine even though membership is now treated as essential to any acceptable Ukraine peace settlement, and proposes a ten-state 'Team Enlargement' coalition led by Germany to convert Chancellor Merz's May 2026 associate-membership letter into a formal framework endorsed at the October and December 2026 European Councils, before France's 2027 election cycle freezes all decision-making.

insights.claim: EU membership is highly likely to be essential to any Ukraine peace settlement that Kyiv would accept, America has made clear it sees Ukrainian membership as an indispensable element of such a settlement, and Ukraine is pushing to join as early as 2027.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: EU accession is now a war-termination variable rather than a slow bureaucratic process — timelines for Ukrainian reconstruction and market integration compress accordingly.
insights.quote: The EU lacks a strategy to get Ukraine quickly and safely through the door.
insights.locator: Time to move

insights.claim: The opportunity for a new enlargement framework shrinks as months pass because France's 2027 electoral cycle will freeze enlargement discussions and decision-making, as will elections in other member states in the second half of 2026 and 2027.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: A hard political deadline: anything not agreed by roughly end-2026 slips past the French cycle, pushing real accession progress into the late 2020s.
insights.quote: France’s 2027 electoral cycle will freeze discussions and decision-making around enlargement
insights.locator: Conclusion

insights.claim: Member states have not yet converged around a single strategy, and the authors' blunt judgement is that the moment to move is now or enlargement may never happen.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Frames enlargement as a binary near-term outcome, not a gradient — relevant to anyone pricing Ukrainian, Moldovan or Western Balkans convergence trades.
insights.quote: The moment to move is now; or enlargement may never happen.
insights.locator: Member states have not yet converged

insights.claim: None of the candidate countries, with the possible exception of Montenegro, is ready to join the EU today, which means the binding constraint is EU internal preparation of institutions, politics and publics rather than candidate readiness alone.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Montenegro is the near-term test case; the EU's own reform bottleneck is the variable to watch, not candidate compliance metrics.
insights.locator: While none of the candidate countries

insights.claim: Failing to integrate candidate countries bordering the bloc represents a growing vulnerability in economic, political and strategic terms, and European leaders largely understand the geopolitical imperative — where they hesitate is over how to make it work in practice.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: The blockage is implementation design, not political will at leader level — so watch technical framework documents, not summit rhetoric, for signal.
insights.quote: Can the EU successfully enlarge without overstretching itself?
insights.locator: It is time for the EU to move forward decisively

insights.claim: The European Commission presented member states with three options at a Brussels dinner in March 2026: the status quo merit-based process, 'enhanced gradual integration' linking progressive policy access to negotiation clusters, and 'phased integration' or reverse enlargement that would make Ukraine a political member before it fulfils all criteria.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: These three options bound the design space; which one prevails determines when Ukraine gains single-market and funding access.
insights.locator: Getting on the front foot

insights.claim: The Commission found little support for reverse enlargement, with one EU official saying 'this presented the real unity of member states', and member state representatives pushed back hard at the Commission developing proposals without engaging them first.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Reverse enlargement is effectively dead; member-state-authored models are the only live path, which slows the process but makes outcomes more durable.
insights.quote: “this presented the real unity of member states”
insights.locator: But the commission found little support

insights.claim: France floated 'an integrated state status' granted by a European Council decision that would open all accession negotiations and provide access to EU funds available to third countries, while Austria drove a separate proposal through the informal Friends of Western Balkans group.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Multiple competing status categories are being invented; the winning label determines which EU funding lines candidates can actually draw on.
insights.locator: Merz’s letter

insights.claim: The most influential proposal is German chancellor Friedrich Merz's May letter to European institutional leaders proposing associate membership for Ukraine — a presence in the European Council, Commission and Parliament without voting rights, while retaining full membership as the eventual aim.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: The specific mechanism most likely to become policy — voting-rights exclusion is the concession that unlocks sceptic member states.
insights.quote: The proposal was unlike anything suggested for an accession country before.
insights.locator: But the most influential proposal came in May

insights.claim: Officials regard the Merz letter as the most compelling proposal on the table and perhaps the only one with a realistic chance of building consensus, though it has yet to be developed into a full concept.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Concentration of official expectation on a single undeveloped document is itself a fragility — the concept's drafting is the next decision point.
insights.locator: Among those most closely involved in planning

insights.claim: The Merz letter's four principles are that associate membership is an interim step toward full membership, that candidates must fulfil the criteria to become fully-fledged members, that access to funds reserved for EU states is denied until full membership, and that reversibility applies should a country regress.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: The four principles are the negotiating template — 'no funds before full membership' is the clause that protects existing cohesion and CAP recipients.
insights.locator: Germany would be a key player

insights.claim: The Hungarian general election in the first half of 2026 led Budapest to lift its veto over starting accession talks for Ukraine, after which the European Council agreed to open the first cluster on fundamentals for both Ukraine and Moldova.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: The single biggest procedural unlock of 2026 has already happened — accession negotiations are formally live for Ukraine and Moldova.
insights.locator: One major change in the first half of 2026

insights.claim: Merz and Macron institutionalised their joint Franco-German enlargement proposal at their ministerial council meeting on 17 July, called on the EU to push for internal reforms, and trailed an in-depth discussion at the October council meeting.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: The Franco-German axis is aligned and has a dated forum — the October European Council is the near-term catalyst to watch.
insights.locator: Merz and Macron further institutionalised

insights.claim: German federal foreign minister Johann Wadephul's May 2026 six points on Germany's role in Europe began with forming coalitions of member states around topics where consensus cannot be found among all 27, giving the Team Enlargement approach explicit doctrinal backing in Berlin.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Berlin has formally adopted coalition-of-the-willing methods over EU27 consensus — a structural shift in how EU policy will get made.
insights.locator: A Team Enlargement coalition also aligns

themes.theme: The three-cluster map of member states

insights.claim: Denmark, Germany and Sweden form the 'principled conditionalists' whose genuine support is calibrated by insistence on merit-based accession, rule of law and institutional quality, and who fear enlargement without control rather than enlargement itself.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: This cluster supplies the legitimacy and is the bridge-builder — its conditions define what any workable framework must include.
insights.quote: the principled conditionalists may not fear enlargement itself, but they do fear enlargement without control
insights.locator: Principled conditionalists (Denmark, Germany and Sweden)

insights.claim: Austria, France, Italy and the Netherlands are 'conditional sceptics' whose real support is gated by specific national concerns — decision-making safeguards for France, fiscal prudence for the Netherlands, migration for Italy and Austria — and who are unlikely ever to become enlargement enthusiasts but can be bought off with reassurance.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Each sceptic has a nameable price; enumerating them is the practical roadmap to a qualified majority.
insights.quote: They do not respond well to moralising and share many of the ideas and worries of the principled conditionalists—they have a pragmatic approach that emphasises practical gains, control, predictability and risk management.
insights.locator: Conditional sceptics (Austria, France, Italy and the Netherlands)

insights.claim: Lithuania and Poland are 'security maximalists' whose support is urgency-driven and anchored in existential threat perception of Russia, which may make them creative and open to interim solutions for candidate states.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: The frontline states are the flexibility reservoir — they will accept imperfect interim statuses that others would reject as unprincipled.
insights.locator: Security maximalists (Lithuania and Poland)

insights.claim: Hungary under prime minister Peter Magyar will not obstruct Ukraine's accession and financial support as Viktor Orban did, which means some member states may now have to reveal their own sceptical positions because Budapest no longer provides a convenient shield.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Removing the designated blocker exposes latent opposition — expect previously quiet capitals to start voicing conditions.
insights.quote: Moreover, with Budapest no longer providing a convenient shield, some member states may increasingly have to reveal their own rather sceptical positions on enlargement.
insights.locator: The outlier, comprising Hungary

insights.claim: The only genuine common ground across all ten member states including Hungary is merit-based conditionality, which the authors call the glue holding the group together, with disagreement centring on what merit means in practice and how fast the bar can be cleared.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Any proposal that dilutes conditionality loses the coalition; the negotiation will be over definitions and pace, not principles.
insights.quote: it is the glue that holds this group together
insights.locator: The only genuine common ground

insights.claim: The main unresolved tension that could keep the coalition divided is whether Ukraine becomes a member first with Western Balkans states coming later, though a new approach open to all candidates could defuse it.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Queue-jumping is the fault line — Western Balkans states and their EU sponsors will trade support for parallel treatment.
insights.locator: What could keep the group divided

themes.theme: Public opinion and the migration frame

insights.claim: Migration is the top enlargement concern in the latest EU barometer on attitudes toward enlargement at 40 per cent, followed by corruption and organised crime at 39 per cent and cost to European taxpayers at 37 per cent.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Three concerns cluster within three points of each other — messaging must address all three, not pick one.
insights.locator: Controlling migration

insights.claim: Mobility concerns are driven more by Schengen arrangements and transition periods than by accession itself, and parts of the accession process — specifically Chapter 24 on Justice and Home Affairs — are aimed at preventing migrants transiting through candidate countries, yet enlargement-sceptic countries still invoke uncontrolled migration to slow-walk accession.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: The dominant public objection is technically misplaced, meaning it is a political rather than substantive obstacle and can in principle be neutralised by communication.
insights.quote: Still, enlargement-sceptic countries refer to the issue of uncontrolled migration to slow-walk accession.
insights.locator: Although mobility concerns are driven

insights.claim: Public support for enlargement varies sharply across the ten: 79 per cent in Sweden, 75 per cent in Denmark, 74 per cent in Lithuania, 70 per cent in Poland, 69 per cent in the Netherlands, 64 per cent in Hungary, 53 per cent in Italy, 49 per cent in Germany, 45 per cent in Austria and 43 per cent in France.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Germany at 49 per cent and France at 43 per cent are the weak links precisely where leadership is required — the numbers explain the political caution.
insights.locator: This generally positive stance is strongly reflected

insights.claim: In Austria 47 per cent express concern about uncontrolled migration arising from future enlargement, with similar figures in Denmark, France, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Lithuania, the Netherlands, Poland and Sweden.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Migration anxiety is uniform across the coalition regardless of headline enlargement support — it is the one message every capital must handle.
insights.locator: In Austria 47% of people express concern

insights.claim: The enlargement debate has so far remained confined to policy circles, and the lack of conversation with domestic audiences leaves fertile ground for populist and far-right narratives framing enlargement as a driver of migration, a fiscal burden and an importer of instability.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: First-mover advantage in framing has not yet been claimed; the side that starts communicating first sets the terms.
insights.quote: The enlargement debate has so far remained confined to policy circles.
insights.locator: The enlargement debate has so far remained confined

insights.claim: ECFR polling shows a big chunk of European voters have yet to make up their mind about enlargement, leaving space for opinions to move either way.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Public opinion is not yet locked, which is the entire premise for the paper's narrative-work recommendation.
insights.locator: ECFR polling shows that a big chunk of European voters

themes.theme: Money: funds, CAP and the MFF

insights.claim: Fears that new members' financial demands will reduce existing members' cohesion funding centre on the common agricultural policy because of Ukraine's massive agricultural potential, and the Commission's new multi-annual financial framework proposal omits any allocated funds for new members.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: The MFF omission is a concrete signal that Ukrainian accession is being designed to avoid triggering a CAP and cohesion fight — watch agricultural lobbies in France, Poland and Italy.
insights.locator: Denying access to membership funds before full accession

insights.claim: Since the recommencement of Russian aggression in 2022 the Commission has increased pre-accession funds for the Western Balkans, Moldova and Ukraine, and the growth plan for the Western Balkans aims to integrate those countries into the single market and deepen EU-related reform.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Single-market integration is already being delivered through pre-accession instruments ahead of formal membership — the real convergence trade is live now.
insights.locator: Since the recommencement of Russian aggression

insights.claim: In June, Belgium, France, Germany, Luxembourg and the Netherlands proposed that accession treaties include a new blueprint to support 'sustained progress after enlargement', so the framework can be insulated from Orban-style rule of law regression after new members join.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Post-accession reversibility clauses are the innovation that makes enlargement politically saleable — a structural change to what EU membership means.
insights.locator: Applying safeguards and reversibility

themes.theme: American transactionalism as an enlargement risk

insights.claim: American transactionalism is eroding the very conditions candidate countries must meet to join the EU even as Washington still expects Ukraine to become a member, and in the Western Balkans Washington has actively undermined EU rule of law conditionality by engaging with illiberal leaders and lifting sanctions previously placed on them.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: The US is simultaneously demanding and obstructing the outcome — a contradiction that raises execution risk on any Balkans accession timeline.
insights.locator: In candidate states, America’s transactionalism

insights.claim: US focus on making money for American business has produced episodes such as the EU ambassador to Bosnia and Herzegovina warning that US antics were jeopardising the country's EU accession process.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Commercial US engagement in the Balkans now carries a documented accession cost — a specific channel through which US-EU friction hits regional integration.
insights.locator: Its focus on making money for American business

insights.claim: Trump's return to power and the deepening ideological links between MAGA-aligned actors and European far-right parties have given related European movements a renewed sense of confidence and legitimacy, adding to the fear among decision-makers of handing ammunition to populists or facing divisive national referendums on accession.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Transatlantic political contagion is a direct input to EU enlargement risk — referendum risk in any single member state can stall the whole process.
insights.locator: Trump’s return to power

insights.claim: A leader of Poland's nationalist far-right Confederation party recently argued Poland should block Ukrainian accession over historical disputes including a military unit name controversy and Volhynia massacre exhumations, and ECFR polling shows voters of Poland's two far-right parties see Ukraine primarily as a rival or adversary — sentiments shared by supporters of Austria's Freedom Party, Fidesz and Alternative for Germany.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Even in the most pro-Ukraine frontline state, historical grievance is an available veto narrative — Polish domestic politics is a real accession risk factor.
insights.locator: Just recently, a leader of the nationalist far-right

insights.claim: Step one is for Germany, supported by the security maximalists and principled conditionalists, to turn the Merz letter into a fully developed enlargement concept structured around merit-based conditionality, no access to certain funds before full membership, safeguards and reversibility, and migration — with Hungary handled through veto-risk mitigation rather than concept-shaping.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: A specific, dated deliverable due before the October 2026 European Council — the first checkpoint against which to judge whether this plan is real.
insights.locator: Step one—Agree to develop the “Merz letter”

insights.claim: Step three has the coalition propose the framework as a formal position in the General Affairs Council ahead of the October 2026 European Council for endorsement there, with the Irish presidency then using the December 2026 European Council to agree political conclusions endorsing it.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Two dated European Council decision points in Q4 2026 are the concrete catalysts for anyone tracking EU enlargement policy.
insights.locator: Step three—Secure endorsement by the European Council

insights.claim: Step four applies the framework throughout 2027 to candidates Albania, Moldova, Montenegro and Ukraine, with Montenegro's accession treaty providing the first opportunity to test it and potentially acting as a final membership contract as Montenegro joins.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Montenegro is the proof-of-concept accession; its treaty terms will set the template every later candidate inherits.
insights.locator: Step four—Put the new framework into practice

insights.claim: Rather than promoting a single rigid vision, the authors argue a broad European narrative should let each member state emphasise the aspects most relevant to its domestic realities — credibility for the principled conditionalists, manageability for the conditional sceptics, security for the maximalists — because a single grand rigid vision could be counterproductive.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Deliberately fragmented messaging over a common framework is the political technology being proposed — a template for any multi-jurisdiction policy rollout.
insights.locator: Step two—Share a new narrative on enlargement

insights.claim: Candidate states are told they must go beyond formal accession requirements and adapt to a far more politicised environment inside the EU — showing openness to safeguards, transitional arrangements and migration management mechanisms, and taking their case directly to member state publics through citizens' dialogues, town halls, business roadshows and investment forums outside capital cities.
insights.speaker: Engjellushe Morina, Gabrielė Valodskaitė
insights.so_what: Accession has become a public-relations and lobbying campaign, not only a compliance exercise — candidate governments' communications capacity is now a variable.
insights.locator: Work more closely with candidate states
